newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 3.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Irish Education minister Niamh Breathnach on Monday faced the prospect of industrial action at primary and third level education as the new school year got under way.
- Irish actor Liam Neeson, star of the Neil Jordan epic "Michael Collins', has had emergency surgery in Italy where he fell ill after the film's premiere at the Venice Film Festival.
- Wexford was in flames as bonfires of celebration blazed for the county's new All-Ireland hurling champions.

- Up to 40,000 new jobs could be created in Ireland by the year 2010 as a direct result of investment in advanced telecommunications, according to a new report on communications and enterprise commissioned by Forfas, the advisory board on industrial development.
- The Irish government's failure to introduce 80 recommendations of the 1994 Small Business Task Force was slammed on Monday by Mary O'Rourke, deputy leader of the opposition party Fianna Fail.
- A Presbyterian minister it is a "sad comment" that representative of the Protestant churches are still holding office in sectarian organisations such as the Orange Order.

- Both sides in the Dunnes Stores dispute were increasingly hopeful on Monday of an early resumption of talks after an all-out picket brought business to a standstill in the company's 73 retail outlets.

- Morgan Grenfell, which is one of the biggest fund managers in the Dublin's International Financial Services Centre, has suspended dealings in three of its funds pending an investigation into the value of these investments.
